comment: Nuxel on-screen / physical keyboard document (mission area 29, mission area 48 group 'Input'). Installed to /etc/nuxel/keyboard/keyboard.json. Read by tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-keyboard-apply.sh, which either applies a key to a real component on this stack or records the honest reason it could not. This file is the document the Nuxel Settings app writes (pwa/nuxel-apps/settings/settings-model.js, DOCS.keyboard) and the document nuxelctl writes, so the UI and the console share ONE settings system.
consumer: tools/s10plus/a33/nuxel-keyboard-apply.sh -> the installed OSK provider (stevia / stevia-phosh-osk-provider) through phoc's zwp_text_input_manager_v3, plus the GNOME/GTK input settings the WebKitGTK session reads
probe: keyboard-state (launcher host status.read -> /run/nuxel-keyboard.state, written by the applier)

stack.comment: Inspected on disk, not assumed: the Fedora 43 ARM64 rootfs manifest ships stevia + stevia-phosh-osk-provider as the phosh OSK, and the UTM VM configuration script writes a squeekboard config. The applier therefore probes for BOTH and configures whichever is actually installed; if neither is installed it says so (NO_OSK_INSTALLED) instead of pretending.
stack.alternate_supported: squeekboard (used by the UTM VM image script artifacts/vm/nuxel-aarch64.utm/scripts/phosh-phone-resolution.sh)
stack.text_input_protocol: zwp_text_input_manager_v3 (phoc / wlroots); WebKitGTK focuses a text field -> the compositor raises the OSK, no app-side IPC required
stack.fallback: an in-page key pad is allowed ONLY as a labelled last resort (Terminal already carries one); it is never reported as the system keyboard

keyboard.haptics_intensity_comment: low=subtle (default), medium, high. Only meaningful as genuine amplitude when the actuator exposes a writable strength control; otherwise the daemon reports intensity_mode=duration and this is pulse feel, not amplitude.
